about: Prayers that surround the recitation of Śrī Rudram but are not part of TS 4.5 or 4.7. Shown apart from the numbered anuvākas, each with its source; never analysed as the canonical text.

items.label: Invocation
items.source: Recited before the Namakam, and in the Mahānyāsa (T. M. Nārāyaṇaśāstrī’s edition, Śāradāvilāsa, Kumbakonam, as transcribed in the vishvAsa corpus: taittirIyam/sUtram/ApastambaH/gRhyam/paddhatiH/rudra-prashna-mahAnyAsaH). Not part of the Taittirīya Saṃhitā.
items.translation: Om. Homage to the blessed Rudra.

items.place: in some recitations, within the Namakam
items.label: नमस्ते अस्तु भगवन् …
items.source: A later prayer of praise (‘namaste astu bhagavan viśveśvarāya …’) that some traditions recite with the Namakam. It is not in the Taittirīya Saṃhitā; the previous page printed it inside Anuvāka 1. None of the witnesses used for this edition contains it, so its text is not reproduced here until it can be checked against a printed source.

items.label: Tryambaka mantra
items.source: Taittirīya Saṃhitā, prapāṭhaka 1.8 (W1, the same edition as the base text). Not part of TS 4.5.11, where the previous page printed it.
items.translation: We worship the three-eyed one, fragrant, increaser of prosperity. Like a cucumber from its stalk, may I be freed from death — not from immortality.

items.place: after the Chamakam, in many recitations
items.label: इडा देवहूः …
items.text: इडा॑ देव॒हूर्मनु॑र्यज्ञ॒नीर्बृह॒स्पति॑रुक्थाम॒दानि॑ शँसिष॒द्विश्वे॑ दे॒वाः [3] सू॒क्त॒वाच॒ᳶ पृथि॑वि मात॒र्मा मा॑ हिँसी॒र्मधु॑ मनिष्ये॒ मधु॑ जनिष्ये॒ मधु॑ वक्ष्यामि॒ मधु॑ वदिष्यामि॒ मधु॑मतीन्दे॒वेभ्यो॒ वाच॑मुद्यासँ शुश्रू॒षेण्या॑म्मनु॒ष्ये॑भ्य॒स्तम्मा॑ दे॒वा अ॑वन्तु शो॒भायै॑ पि॒तरोऽनु॑ मदन्तु ॥
items.source: Taittirīya Saṃhitā 3.3.2 (W1, the same edition as the base text). Not part of TS 4.7.
items.translation: Iḍā who calls the gods, Manu who leads the sacrifice, Bṛhaspati shall recite the hymns of praise; the All-gods are the speakers of the hymns. Mother Earth, do not harm me. Sweet shall I think, sweet shall I bring forth, sweet shall I bear, sweet shall I speak; may I utter honeyed speech to the gods, worth hearing to men. May the gods protect me for splendour; may the fathers rejoice after me.

items.label: Śānti
items.source: The customary close of a Vedic recitation. Not part of TS 4.5 or 4.7.
